questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Shakespeare's company performed at which famous London theatre, closely associated with his plays?
options: The Globe Theatre
The Royal Albert Hall
The Old Vic
Sadler's Wells
questions.why: The Globe Theatre, built in 1599, was where Shakespeare's company (the Lord Chamberlain's Men) performed most of his plays. Students sometimes confuse it with modern or unrelated venues.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In Romeo and Juliet, what is the dramatic effect of the play's frequent use of dramatic irony?
options: It lets the audience know more than the characters, building tension as we watch them head toward disaster
It confuses the audience so they cannot follow the plot
It removes all tension because the audience already knows everything the characters know
It is only used for comic relief and has no effect on tension
questions.answer: It lets the audience know more than the characters, building tension as we watch them head toward disaster
questions.why: Dramatic irony works because the audience holds knowledge the characters lack (e.g. Juliet's fake death), creating suspense and tragic tension — not confusion or comedy.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A student claims that fungi like mushrooms can only reproduce sexually. Which fact proves this wrong?
options: Fungi can reproduce asexually by releasing spores that grow into genetically identical fungi
Fungi never reproduce because they are not living organisms
Fungi can only reproduce if two different species combine
Fungi reproduce exclusively through seeds like plants
questions.answer: Fungi can reproduce asexually by releasing spores that grow into genetically identical fungi
questions.why: Many fungi reproduce asexually via spores, producing genetically identical offspring — showing asexual reproduction isn't limited to simple organisms like bacteria.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: What term describes the period in Western Europe roughly between the fall of Rome and the Renaissance?
options: The Middle Ages (medieval period)
The Enlightenment
The Industrial Age
The Bronze Age
questions.why: The Middle Ages spans roughly 476 CE to the 1400s, filled with feudal kingdoms and the Church's power — students sometimes wrongly picture this era as a total blank with nothing happening.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: In the feudal system, what did knights typically provide to their lord in exchange for land?
options: Military service and protection
A yearly cash salary
Farming labour on the lord's fields
Nothing — knights owed no obligations
questions.why: Knights received land (a fief) from lords in return for military service, not wages or farm labour — that mix-up confuses the roles of knights with those of peasants.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which moment in Romeo and Juliet shows the 'love vs hate' theme through violence rather than tenderness?
options: Mercutio's death after Tybalt's sword fight with Romeo
Romeo and Juliet's first meeting at the Capulet ball
The balcony scene where they exchange vows
Juliet's soliloquy waiting for the Nurse's news
questions.answer: Mercutio's death after Tybalt's sword fight with Romeo
questions.why: The street violence between the feuding families (Mercutio's death) shows hate driving the plot toward tragedy, contrasting with the romantic scenes — the theme isn't only expressed through affection.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In an experiment testing how the concentration of salt water affects seed germination, a student mixes up which variable is independent. What is the independent variable here?
options: The concentration of salt water
The number of seeds that germinate
The temperature of the room
The type of soil used
questions.why: The independent variable is what the experimenter deliberately changes — here, salt concentration. Germination rate is the dependent variable, the outcome being measured.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Which statement about the Crusades is false?
options: The Crusades were fought only over religion, with no economic motives whatsoever
The First Crusade aimed to capture Jerusalem for Christendom
Crusader states in the Holy Land were eventually lost
Italian port cities like Venice and Genoa profited from transporting crusaders
questions.answer: The Crusades were fought only over religion, with no economic motives whatsoever
questions.why: The Crusades were driven by a mix of religious zeal, political ambition, and economic opportunity (trade routes, land, wealth) — reducing them to pure religion ignores these other motives.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: Which of these is true about the historical setting in which Shakespeare wrote his plays?
options: Female roles were played by young men or boys, since women were banned from the English stage
Women regularly performed female roles alongside men
Plays were performed with elaborate film-style special effects
Audiences watched silently in fully darkened theatres
questions.answer: Female roles were played by young men or boys, since women were banned from the English stage
questions.why: In Shakespeare's time, women were not permitted to act on the English stage, so boys or young men played female roles like Juliet — a key fact about Elizabethan theatre conventions.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: A student says the Nurse's comic, rambling speech style has no real purpose in Romeo and Juliet. What does this overlook about Shakespeare's use of characterisation and contrast?
options: It provides comic relief and contrasts with the play's tragic tone, making the tragedy hit harder by comparison
It exists only to pad out the play's length
It shows the Nurse is meant to be taken as seriously as Friar Lawrence
It has no connection to the play's themes or structure at all
questions.answer: It provides comic relief and contrasts with the play's tragic tone, making the tragedy hit harder by comparison
questions.why: Shakespeare uses the Nurse's comic chatter to contrast with the tragic elements, heightening the emotional impact of darker scenes through juxtaposition — a deliberate technique, not filler.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A student claims that identical twins are an example of asexual reproduction in humans. What's wrong with this claim?
options: Identical twins result from sexual reproduction (a fertilised egg splitting), not asexual reproduction, which needs only one parent
Identical twins prove humans can reproduce asexually
Identical twins are genetically different, so this claim is about mutation, not reproduction
Identical twins only occur in animals that reproduce asexually
questions.answer: Identical twins result from sexual reproduction (a fertilised egg splitting), not asexual reproduction, which needs only one parent
questions.why: Identical twins come from one fertilised egg (formed by sexual reproduction of two parents) splitting into two embryos — this is genetically similar but still originates from sexual reproduction, not asexual reproduction which requires only one parent.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A classmate says learning about the Crusades is pointless because Europe and the Middle East are 'completely different places now' with no connection to that history. Explain, using your own reasoning and at least one specific long-term effect, why this view misunderstands how historical events shape the present.
